key_insight: Generating extra images does not reliably help AI answer visual questions. Across 13 vision-language model–generator pairs, helper images reduced average accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks.
problem_solved: The study tests whether multimodal AI can improve visual reasoning by generating and consulting a helper image rather than relying only on the original image.
method: Have a model describe the helper image it needs to answer a visual question.
Generate that helper, then answer using both the original and generated images.
Compare accuracy with and without generation across 13 model–generator pairs and ten tasks, including the unified models BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B.
impact: Practitioners should not assume image generation improves visual reasoning: it can reduce accuracy. Evaluate generated-image workflows against a no-generation baseline before adopting them.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: original image + question → helper description → generated image → answer using both images.
Headline metric card: −3.7 percentage points in mean accuracy.
Task-outcome graphic highlighting accuracy declines on nine of ten tasks.
Model comparison cards showing BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B each losing accuracy on eight tasks.
paper_title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
paper_authors: Xueyang Yu, Yifan Jing, Taiming Lu, Linrong Cai, Zhipeng Cai
